sentences.text: Alistipes putredinis was moved out of Bacteroides into the new genus Alistipes, whose members are bile-resistant, pigment-producing, strictly anaerobic Gram-negative rods.
The organisms behind that reclassification were recovered from inflamed and non-inflamed tissue during studies of appendicitis in children.
They resemble the Bacteroides fragilis group in bile resistance and in resistance to vancomycin, kanamycin and colistin, but make brown pigment on blood media.
Further Alistipes species of human origin were later described, differing from Alistipes finegoldii by about three percent in 16S ribosomal RNA sequence.
